body: What would it take to implement a monitor / daemon that plugs into iterm, sees claude sessions that are running, determeins when the cache is going to expire and nudges me with a apple script popup with deep link into terminal window that's cache will expire?

author: claude
body: About half a day, in three small parts. (1) A Claude Code hook that runs after every turn and writes one line per session: when the last request went out, the folder, and the iTerm tab's id. iTerm gives every tab an id (ITERM_SESSION_ID), and I checked it reaches Claude's processes, so the hook knows which tab it is in. (2) A launchd job, like the daily usage snapshot, that wakes every minute and, for a session idle about 55 minutes whose tab is still open, shows a dialog: 'The cache for <folder> runs out in 5 minutes' with a Go there button. (3) Go there tells iTerm by AppleScript to bring up the tab with that id. Two catches: only the main conversation has the 1-hour cache (helpers use 5 minutes and rarely pause), and with several sessions open it could nag, so I'd only nudge for big prompts (over 100k tokens) and stay quiet at night. It should only nudge, never type into the tab for you. Want it built? Say so in the chat, since it installs a hook and a background job.

author: claude
body: Built, installed and tested (hub commit 52a0200, merged). About five minutes before a big session's 1-hour cache runs out, a Mac dialog names the folder and the tab, and Go there brings up that iTerm tab. It only reminds and never types anything. It skips prompts under 100k tokens, 5-minute caches, and 10 pm to 8 am. The live test from the real background job brought up the right tab. The status line also shows 'cache till 11:59 AM (1h)'. Turn it off with make cache-nudge-uninstall; make cache-nudge-status shows what it's doing. Sessions opened before the install pick it up after a restart. One gap is in the backlog: a session waiting on a permission prompt isn't reminded yet.
